title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Fiji: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Fiji: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Fiji: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: When a death occurs in Fiji, official civil registration is governed by the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act (Cap. 49) and administered through the Ministry of Justice Fiji - BDM Registry [1][3]. This checklist organizes the immediate medical, registration, social security, probate, tax, and cross-border steps using official Fijian legislation and agency guidance.

steps.title: Medical certification, emergency liaison, and burial or cremation approval
steps.html:
• Obtain the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD) from the attending physician at the hospital or health facility, or through Coroner inquiries if the death occurred unexpectedly or outside medical care [1][5]. For urgent public health coordination or medical enquiries, contact Ministry of Health and Medical Services Fiji (158 toll-free enquiries; 911 medical emergency) [10].
  • Under the Burial and Cremation Act (Cap. 117) and the Cremation Regulations, no burial or cremation may proceed without statutory authorization and compliance with local sanitary or cremation permit rules, so confirm facility requirements before fixing funeral dates [5].
  • Keep multiple original certified copies of the MCCD and hospital discharge records, because both civil registration and benefit claims depend on primary medical documentation [1][5][6].

steps.title: Civil death registration within the 7-day statutory deadline
steps.html:
• Report and register the death with Ministry of Justice Fiji - BDM Registry within 7 days from the date of death as required under Section 18(1) of the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act (Cap. 49) [1]. Note that the 2-month (60-day) timeframe applies to birth registrations rather than deaths [1].
  • Submit particulars at the nearest BDM office along with the MCCD and the deceased person's identification details, noting amendments enacted under the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration (Amendment) Act 2021 [1][2][3].
  • Initial registration of a death is free of charge; under the Ministry of Justice BDM Registry fee schedule (inclusive of 12.5% VAT), statutory fees are FJD 11.25 VIP for an official Death Certificate ($10.00 VEP + $1.25 VAT) and FJD 5.63 VIP for registry searches and issuance of letters ($5.00 VEP + $0.63 VAT) [4].
  • Request several official Death Certificates immediately for banks, superannuation claims, probate filings, and overseas use [3][4][7][9].

steps.title: Fiji National Provident Fund (FNPF) Special Death Benefit and funeral assistance
steps.html:
• Notify Fiji National Provident Fund (FNPF) promptly to initiate member death benefit settlement [6].
  • Eligible FNPF members carry a Special Death Benefit (SDB) of up to FJD 8,500 in addition to the total member account balance, subject to statutory eligibility conditions including age limits and payment of the annual SDB premium for the applicable financial year [6].
  • Up to FJD 2,000 from the Special Death Benefit can be released quickly as Funeral Assistance (within approximately 20 working days), provided a valid Memorandum of Administration (MOA) is on file and the annual SDB premium was paid [6].
  • If no valid MOA is in place, the funeral assistance portion is not released under that expedited rule, and FNPF distributes eligible funds according to the member's filed nomination schedule or formal estate administration rules [6][8].

steps.title: High Court probate, estate administration, and Fiji Revenue and Customs Service (FRCS)
steps.html:
• Review estate assets against the Succession, Probate and Administration Act (Cap. 60) and Chief Registrar's Practice Direction No. 2 of 1994 before applying to the High Court for Probate or Letters of Administration [7][8].
  • Practice Direction No. 2 of 1994 requires primary original documents (such as the original Will and original Death Certificate) and statutory compliance with estate administration and 21-day creditor notice procedures once administration is granted, rather than an unverified pre-filing newspaper notice rule [7][8].
  • Where institutional administration is needed or appointed under a Will or intestacy, check eligibility with Fiji Public Trustee Corporation Limited (FPTCL) [8].
  • Contact Fiji Revenue and Customs Service (FRCS) to close personal tax registrations, file any final income tax returns, and settle VAT or capital gains obligations if business or real property disposals occur; Fiji does not impose an inheritance or estate tax [8][11].

steps.title: Cross-border Apostille authentication and notifying institutions
steps.html:
• Because Fiji is a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, Fiji Death Certificates and court grants needed by banks, pension funds, or registries abroad are authenticated by Apostille through Fiji's designated Competent Authority, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs [9].
  • Ask foreign receiving authorities whether certified translations or original Apostilled extracts are needed before dispatching documents overseas [9].
  • Notify local banks, insurers, land registries, utility accounts, and employers in writing with certified Death Certificate copies, and settle unpaid final wages or workplace benefits under the Employment Relations Act 2007 and any court grant [7][8][12].

contacts.name: Ministry of Justice Fiji - BDM Registry
contacts.note: Registers deaths within the 7-day statutory deadline under Cap. 49 s. 18(1) and issues certified Death Certificates and extracts under the August 2025 fee schedule.

contacts.name: Fiji National Provident Fund (FNPF)
contacts.note: Administers member balance payouts, Special Death Benefit (up to FJD 8,500), and MOA-conditioned Funeral Assistance (up to FJD 2,000). Short code: 5857.

contacts.name: Ministry of Health and Medical Services Fiji
contacts.note: Toll-free general enquiries 158 (Monday-Friday 8:00-16:30); medical emergency ambulance 911; Central/Eastern (679) 332 0844, Western (679) 666 0411, Northern (679) 881 2522.

contacts.name: Fiji Revenue and Customs Service (FRCS)
contacts.note: Tax authority for final income tax, TIN closure, and capital gains or VAT clearances. Toll-free line within Fiji: 1326.
